turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mrs Dlamini, obs are done. Blood pressure is one eighteen over 76, pulse 96, temperature 37.2, sats 98 percent on air, respiratory rate sixteen. She managed a few sips of water while we waited.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks, Sister. Come through, Mrs Dlamini. What's brought you in today?

[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Ag, Doctor, hectic weekend. My cousin Lindiwe got married in Paarl on Saturday, the dress was something else, and the lamb was lekker, but since Sunday morning my tummy's been running non-stop.
[SEG0004] person_3 (PATIENT): We sat on the N1 forever afterwards, some robot was out by the tunnel, but anyway. It's this diarrhoea. That's the actual thing.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): So it started Sunday morning, after the wedding meal?

[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja. Sunday morning, early. Yesterday I was on the loo, um, I lost count, maybe eight or nine times, something like that. Could've been more, I stopped counting after the rusk.

[SEG0007] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'm Bongi, I stay with her during the week. She was back and forth to the toilet all yesterday, and she vomited too, three times on Sunday and once yesterday morning. Nothing up since then.

[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): I blame the potato salad, hey. My sister Nomsa has the same bug, and two cousins, and Nomsa phoned to say she's turning the corner already. The DJ played till late, shame, my feet are still cross, but that's not why I'm here.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): A few of you off the same plate, then. Any blood in the stool, or black stool?
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): No, no blood. Just watery brown stuff. Horrible, sorry.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Have you felt feverish at all, chills, that sort of thing?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): No, I haven't felt hot. Just washed out. Tired, you know, a bit.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cramps with the diarrhoea?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja, low down in the tummy. They come and go, not terrible. If I sit still it eases a bit.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): And when you stand up, any dizziness?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose... sometimes, not really. I got up quick by the kettle and the room did a tiny spin, but I'm not sure that counts. Probably nothing.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, I won't hang anything on that. Are you getting fluids in?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): Little sips of rooibos. Sometimes they stay down, sometimes not really, I feel iffy. I haven't eaten proper since Sunday, just that one dry rusk.

[SEG0019] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, she took Imodium yesterday, against what they told her. Two capsules, two milligrams each, from the chemist. The sister at the day clinic said don't use that for a food bug, but she swallowed them anyway, and she's had none today because I took the box away.

[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja, I just wanted it to stop. Didn't even help, hey. I won't take another one. The box is still in my bag if you want it, next to my lipstick and the Paarl parking ticket.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Leave the Imodium off completely. With this sort of illness loperamide can trap the germ inside, so it isn't the right move, even though the running is miserable.
[SEG0022] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She does take her blood pressure tablet every morning for her high blood pressure. Amlodipine, five milligrams. She had it today, she doesn't miss it.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good, carry on with the amlodipine as usual. That's a separate issue, and the pressure Sister got is fine.

[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me look. Your mouth is a bit dry. Tummy's soft, mildly tender low down, no guarding, and the bowel sounds are busy. The skin on the back of your hand tents just slightly, so this is mild dehydration, not severe.

[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Putting it together, this is most likely a short gastro from the wedding food, seeing as the others fell ill too. I'm going to send a stool sample off today, and I'd start ciprofloxacin, 500 milligrams twice a day for three days, just to cover a bacterial food poisoning.
[SEG0026] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She's not mad about antibiotics. And Nomsa is already improving with no medicine at all, just tea.

[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja, please not the cipro if you can help it. Years ago it gave me the shakes, when my knee was playing up, whole other saga with the physio in Bellville, never mind. I'd rather avoid it.

[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, that changes it. Scratch the ciprofloxacin, and we won't send the stool today either. No blood, you're not feverish, it's only been a couple of days, and the others are settling. If it's not better in three days, or if you see blood, or you can't keep sips down, then we send a stool sample.

[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): What will actually help is fluid: small sips often, a Rehidrat sachet in a glass of clean water after a loose stool. Skip cooldrink, fruit juice, and the flat Coke idea, they pull water into the bowel. When you feel up to food, stick to dry toast, rice, or banana.

[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Rehidrat, ja, the chemist will have it. My neighbour still swears by flat Coke, I won't listen to her. And can you believe the wedding photos aren't even out, with what that photographer charged.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ja, leave the flat Coke. If it's not better in three days, come back and see me.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): And if I go downhill tonight, do I still wait?
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): No, don't wait it out. Come back here, or go to casualty, if you can't keep even sips down, you stop passing urine, or you feel faint.
[SEG0034] person_1 (NURSE): The pulse of 96 fits with being a little dry. Blood pressure stayed steady while she was sitting. I'll stick the obs slip in the file.
[SEG0035] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'll keep the sips going at home, and the Imodium stays in the cupboard. High up.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): She's strict, Doctor, worse than my mother, and my mother was a school principal in George. Anyway. Will I be right for church on Sunday? There's a bazaar.

[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Maybe, if the tummy settles, but don't promise the bazaar. No antibiotic from me, and no stool test today. We only send a sample if it's not settling in three days or if there's blood. Fluids, and keep the amlodipine going.
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): So the Rehidrat after each run, little sips, no juice. Ja, I can do that. I'm done with that potato salad.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's the plan. Anything else worrying you before you go?
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): Only that I might have left the wedding gift in the car boot, the vase. Ag, Bongi will remember. I'm fine otherwise, just this tummy.
[SEG0041] person_4 (CAREGIVER): The vase is at home, don't stress. Doctor, if the stool is still watery on Friday I bring her back, ja?
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Exactly. Friday is about three days. If it's not better by then, come back, and we'll send the stool. Sooner if she worsens.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): Sorted. Thanks, Doctor, and thanks Sister. Next wedding I'm eating before I leave the house.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Go gently. See you if you need us.

spec.situation: Diarrhoea and vomiting after a trip or a wedding meal; others at the event are ill; patient counts bowel movements loosely; takes loperamide against advice; mild dehydration signs; stool test conditional; advice on fluids.
features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

omissions.text: Denied black stool/melena when specifically asked ('No, no blood. Just watery brown stuff').
Watery brown stool character of the diarrhoea was stated.
Possible mild dizziness on standing was reported: a brief tiny spin when standing up quickly by the kettle; doctor noted not to rely on it.
Reduced oral intake/poor fluid tolerance details: only little sips of rooibos, sometimes stay down and sometimes not; had not eaten proper food since Sunday except one dry rusk.
Patient tolerated a few sips of water while waiting.
Medication intolerance/adverse reaction to ciprofloxacin was reported: years ago it 'gave me the shakes', leading to decision to avoid it.
Initial plan to start ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily for 3 days for presumed bacterial food poisoning was discussed, then explicitly cancelled after the adverse reaction history.
Doctor changed the initial plan and decided not to send a stool sample today because there was no blood, no fever, only a couple of days of illness, and others were improving.
Mild dehydration was explicitly described as not severe.
Rehidrat sachet dosing instruction was specific: one sachet in a glass of clean water after a loose stool.
Nurse noted blood pressure stayed steady while sitting.
Follow-up timing was concretised as Friday being about three days; caregiver was told to bring her back then if still watery.
